_comment: Copy to watch_rules.json next to server.py and edit. The real file is gitignored. Everything a rule does not set is taken from 'defaults', so a working rule is three or four lines. Placeholders are ${name}; an unknown one is left in the text as-is, so a typo is visible instead of silently empty. An UPPERCASE $NAME in url, headers, proxy or body is expanded from the environment (.env) when the file is loaded - keep tokens, chat ids and proxy passwords there, not here. If every receiver needs the same proxy, move it into 'defaults'; if some receivers are on the LAN, keep it per rule.

rules._comment: Remote access into the home network: the event carries the user, the source IP and the address handed out.
rules.message: VPN-подключение к домашней сети: ${m2} (${m1}) с адреса ${m3}

rules._comment: Settings were saved. Fires on this server's own write tools too - they save the same way and the log does not say who asked. A change made from the router CLI or through ndmc writes 'saving (cli)' instead and is not matched here.
rules.message: На роутере сохранена конфигурация (веб-конфигуратор или RCI)

rules._comment: Web-configurator and RCI logins. Requires authentication logging, which is OFF by default: run 'ip http log auth' then 'system configuration save' in the router CLI (from an Entware shell: ndmc -c '...'). 'exclude' drops this server's own logins - they come from the router's own LAN address - and any other client of your own; adjust the addresses to your network. Cooldown for a log rule is per rule, not per address, so keep it short: with a long one a stranger logging in right after you is swallowed silently.
rules.match: Scgi::Auth::Handler: opened session for user "([^"]+)" from "([^"]+)"
rules.message: Вход в веб-конфигуратор: пользователь ${m1} с адреса ${m2}

rules._comment: Failed logins. Same switch as above; without it a wrong password looks exactly like nothing happening.
rules.message: НЕУДАЧНАЯ попытка входа в веб-конфигуратор: пользователь ${m1} с адреса ${m2}

rules._comment: Brute-force protection kicking in. Needs no switch - bans are logged by default. Stock policy is five attempts in three minutes and a fifteen-minute ban; see lockout-policy in the running config.
rules.match: BfdManager: "([^"]+)": ban remote host ([0-9.]+) for ([0-9]+) minutes
rules.message: Защита от перебора: адрес ${m2} заблокирован на ${m3} мин (служба ${m1})
Незнакомое устройство в сети: ${mac}, IP ${ip}, имя '${name}', hostname '${hostname}', сеть ${interface_name}

rules._comment: Straight to the Telegram Bot API instead of a webhook. api.telegram.org is unreachable directly from this router, so it goes through the same proxy Home Assistant uses. Put all three in .env: TG_TOKEN, TG_CHAT_ID and TG_PROXY=http://user:pass@host:port - the proxy demands authentication (a bare CONNECT gets 407). Only UPPERCASE names are read from the environment. Enable this or the webhook rule, not both.
rules.message: VPN-подключение к домашней сети: ${m2} (${m1}) с адреса ${m3}
